description: Four commercially available CAP devices (two medical, two cosmetic), based on dielectric barrier discharge (DBD) concepts (volume and surface discharge) were investigated in a controlled in vivo study on ten healthy volunteers. Skin barrier related parameters were assessed using transepidermal water loss (TEWL) and electrical impedance at 1 kHz. Skin hydration and microcirculation were employed to capture additional plasma-induced effects. From: C. Hellwig et al. 2026 Skin Research and Technology [Under Review]

distribution.name: skin.hydration.all.devices.raw.data.csv
distribution.description: Skin hydration data measured for all devices, categorized as follows: before plasma treatment (before CAP), immediately after plasma treatment (after CAP), and 30 minutes after plasma treatment (after CAP 2).

distribution.name: skin.impedance.1kHz.all.devices.csv
distribution.description: The data analysis in the paper focused on the impedance amplitude values at 1 kHz (|Z1kHz|), which are listed in this file for all four devices. Impedance at this frequency is predominantly influenced by the SC and minimally affected by deeper skin layers, allowing assessment of SC-specific electrical properties.

distribution.name: TEWL.all.devices.csv
distribution.description: TEWL dataset for all four plasma devices, organized by subject and comprising n = 30 measurements at treated and reference sites before treatment (before CAP), immediately after treatment (after CAP 1), and every 2.5 minutes up to 36.5 minutes (after CAP 13) following CAP treatment.

distribution.name: TEWL.time.progression.mean.all.devices.csv
distribution.description: Mean TEWL time-progression data for all plasma devices, averaged per subject and separated into treated and reference sites, including the corresponding standard deviations.
